Biodiversity is still threatened: wildlife trafficking is a serious problem, and hydropower dams fragment forest ecosystems in the Central Highlands.
laws.penalty: Illegal logging in protected forests: up to 15 years imprisonment under Criminal Code. Wildlife trafficking in forest areas: up to 15 years. Illegal land clearing of forest: heavy fines and criminal prosecution.
exceptions: Community forests managed by ethnic minority villages may use traditional resource extraction
Commercial timber plantations on designated 'production forest' land permitted
Firewood collection in 'protection forest' buffer zones permitted under local regulations
laws.sourceLabel: Bộ Nông nghiệp và Phát triển nông thôn — Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development

quiz.q: What remarkable environmental achievement has Vietnam accomplished regarding forest cover?
options: Forest cover increased from 29% to 42% between 1990 and 2020 through logging bans and reforestation programs — against the trend in most developing Asia
Vietnam protected 100% of its remaining old-growth forests
Vietnam exported more reforestation expertise than any other developing nation
quiz.explanation: Vietnam's forest recovery from 29% (1990) to 42% (2020) is one of developing Asia's remarkable environmental success stories — most countries in the region continued net deforestation during this period. Key policies: a 1997 ban on commercial logging of natural forests, and mass tree planting programs ('5 million hectare program'). However, much recovery is timber plantations rather than biodiverse natural forest — quality matters as much as quantity.

laws.title: Luật Doanh nghiệp Nhà nước — State-Owned Enterprise Law
laws.subtitle: Managing Vietnam's large state enterprise sector
laws.fullDescription: Vietnam's state-owned enterprise (SOE) sector remains large despite 'equitization' (privatization) since the 1990s. Vietnam's largest companies are SOEs: PetroVietnam (oil and gas), Viettel (telecommunications, largest army-owned company), Vietnam Airlines, Electricity of Vietnam (EVN). SOEs remain dominant in energy, banking, telecoms, and strategic sectors. The equitization program has slowed significantly since the late 2000s. SOE managers face conflicts between state objectives (maintaining employment, strategic goals) and commercial performance. Corruption in SOEs has been a major anti-corruption campaign target — multiple SOE executives sentenced to long terms. Vietnam's Committee for Management of State Capital (CMSC) oversees large SOEs.
laws.penalty: SOE directors causing state losses through incompetence or negligence: criminal prosecution ('causing economic damage to the state' offense). Corruption in SOEs: death penalty if embezzlement exceeds ₫1B.
exceptions: Policy-directed SOE activities (maintaining strategic reserve, public service obligations) not subject to commercial performance standard
Military enterprises (Viettel, defense factories) have national security exemptions from standard disclosures
SOEs in natural monopoly sectors (water, power transmission) subject to price regulation rather than competition
laws.sourceLabel: Ủy ban Quản lý vốn nhà nước — Committee for Management of State Capital

quiz.q: What unusual type of company is Viettel — Vietnam's largest telecommunications company?
options: A US-Vietnamese joint venture from the 1990s liberalization
A company owned by the Vietnamese army (Ministry of National Defence) — one of the world's largest military-owned commercial enterprises
A former state enterprise privatized and now publicly listed
A cooperative owned by Vietnam's telecommunications workers
quiz.explanation: Viettel is owned by the Vietnamese Ministry of National Defence — making it one of the world's largest military-owned commercial enterprises. It operates not just in Vietnam but in 10+ countries across Africa, Asia, and Latin America (Telcel in Cambodia, Natcom in Haiti, etc.). A military company competing internationally in civilian telecommunications markets is extremely unusual globally — a distinctive feature of Vietnam's post-1986 Đổi Mới economic model where the military entered commercial activities.
